title: Bones of the lower limb (anterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Large bone of the pelvic girdle, formed by the fusion of the ilium, ischium, and pubis at the acetabulum.
Sacrum at the sacroiliac joint, the other hip bone at the pubic symphysis, and the head of the femur at the acetabulum.
Iliac crest, anterior superior iliac spine, acetabulum, obturator foramen, ischial spine, ischial tuberosity, greater and lesser sciatic notches.
Bone of the thigh; the longest bone of the body.
Acetabulum of the hip bone above; the tibia and the patella at the knee.
Head, neck, greater and lesser trochanters, linea aspera, medial and lateral condyles, adductor tubercle.
hy: A fracture of the neck of the femur can tear the branches of the medial circumflex femoral artery that supply the head, and the head may then die (avascular necrosis).

rows: Sesamoid bone in the tendon of quadriceps femoris, in front of the knee joint; the largest sesamoid bone of the body.
Base above and apex below. The patellar ligament runs from the apex to the tibial tuberosity.
Medial and larger bone of the leg. It carries the weight of the body from the femur to the foot.
Condyles of the femur above, the fibula at its upper and lower ends, and the talus at the ankle.
Medial and lateral condyles, tibial tuberosity, anterior border (the shin), soleal line, medial malleolus.
Slender lateral bone of the leg. It carries little weight and mainly gives attachment to muscles.
Tibia at its upper and lower ends, and the talus, where its lower end forms the lateral malleolus.
hy: The common fibular (peroneal) nerve winds around the neck of the fibula. A fracture or pressure there causes foot drop.

rows: The seven bones of the back half of the foot, between the leg and the metatarsals.
Talus, calcaneus, navicular, cuboid, and the medial, intermediate, and lateral cuneiforms.
The five long bones of the foot between the tarsal bones and the toes, numbered 1 to 5 from the great toe.
Each has a base, a shaft, and a head. The first is the shortest and thickest. The fifth has a tuberosity on its base where fibularis brevis inserts.
